newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shekel sharply lower against mark, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israel shekel sharply lower against mark, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell sharply against the mark and basket of foreign currencies on Monday following the dollar's decline abroad on Friday, dealers said.

"The shekel remained stable against the dollar despite the dollar's fall abroad on Friday. Whenever the shekel reached 3.52 shekels per dollar investors started buying dollars," said Zahi Elias at Bank Leumi.
The shekel's decline against the basket reflected the rise of the European currencies and yen against the dollar, Elias said.

He said volume was low, adding that the release of a relatively high July consumer price index (CPI) on Friday had no impact on trading. "Investors did not react to the CPI figure despite expectations the Bank of Isreal would raise its key lending rate soon," he said.
July's CPI rose 1.0 percent against a rise of 1.1 pct in June.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5220 shekels compared with 3.5200 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7666 against 3.7489 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9864 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9717 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9365 shekels compared with 1.9091 on Friday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5220 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x238 DMG TCC
